title: I went to Bagan once, long ago
title_target: ပုဂံ ရောက်ဖူးခဲ့တယ် — ba.gaⁿ yowk-hpoo:-hkè.-dè
goal: Talking about the past accurately — and facing the hardest unit in this book: ခဲ့ is not a required past-tense marker, and using it everywhere actually makes your sentences wrong.
bekal: telling about past events without changing the verb
using ခဲ့ only where it's really needed
telling ခဲ့ apart from ဖူး and from ပြီ
using time words for the past
telling the story of a trip in a few sentences in a row

dialogs.intro: Ani has just come back from Bagan and tells Mya Mya about it. This is the hardest unit in the book, so read the dialogue twice: once for the story, and once more noticing which sentences use ခဲ့ and which don't.

grammars.title: ⚠️ ခဲ့ is NOT a required past-tense marker
body: This is the hardest part of the unit, and the most common mistake of people who've been learning for a few months. Because English marks the past on every verb, many beginners hear about ခဲ့ and then use it in **every** past sentence. The result is wrong.

head: Sentence
Say it
Correct?
Why
rows: မနေ့က ဈေး သွားတယ်
the past is already marked by မနေ့က
မနေ့က ဈေး သွားခဲ့တယ်
ခဲ့ is overkill for yesterday
ငယ်ငယ်တုန်းက ရောက်ခဲ့တယ်
a distant time, now cut off
ဘာတွေ လုပ်ခဲ့လဲ
asking about a whole series of events now over

after: The rule: **တယ် is enough for almost every past sentence.** Add ခဲ့ only when you want to stress that the event is **distant and closed** — childhood, years ago, a situation that no longer holds.

Compare these two sentences: လူ မများဘူး means "there aren't many people" (now). လူ မများခဲ့ဘူး means "there weren't many people back then" — implying that **now there are many**. That's ခဲ့'s job: marking that the situation has since changed.
When in doubt, **just leave ခဲ့ out**. A sentence without ခဲ့ is almost never wrong; a sentence with an unneeded ခဲ့ always sounds forced.

grammars.title: ခဲ့, ဖူး, and ပြီ — three markers with different jobs
body: All three have to do with the past, but each answers a different question. This table puts them side by side so their jobs are clear.

head: Word
Say it
Answers the question
Example
rows: when? — back then, in a closed-off time
ငယ်ငယ်တုန်းက ရောက်ခဲ့တယ်
already or not yet? — the situation changed
did once, a long time ago
ရောက်ခဲ့ဖူးတယ်

after: ⚠️ Notice that **ခဲ့ and ဖူး can be used together**, and the order is always ခဲ့ first, then ဖူး: ရောက်ခဲ့ဖူးတယ် (I went there once, long ago). Swapping the order is wrong.

grammars.title: …တုန်းက — at that time, when
body: တုန်းက (*tohⁿ:-ga.*) marks a single point in the past, and it's almost always where ခဲ့ turns up in the same sentence.

head: Burmese
Say it
Meaning
rows: ငယ်ငယ်တုန်းက
အဲဒီတုန်းက
ကျောင်းသားဘဝတုန်းက
ပုဂံ ရောက်တုန်းက

after: Keep it apart from **…ကတည်းက** (unit 16), which means "since" and says that the situation is **still going on**. တုန်းက marks a single point that is past and over.

grammars.title: Time words for the past
body: Because the verb ending doesn't tell time, these words carry the whole load. Learn this list and you can talk about anything that's already happened.

head: Burmese
Say it
Meaning
rows: ပြီးခဲ့တဲ့ အပတ်

after: ⚠️ Notice **ပြီးခဲ့တဲ့** — here ခဲ့ appears inside the time word itself, not on the main verb. So ပြီးခဲ့တဲ့အပတ် ဈေး သွားတယ် is already complete: the time word uses ခဲ့, the main verb doesn't need it.

sections.title: Telling the story of a trip in five sentences

blocks.text: Telling about something that has already happened is the peak of A1. You can fill the five-sentence frame below with any trip — out of town, back home, or to the market last week.

head: Part
Burmese
Say it
rows: ပြီးခဲ့တဲ့ အပတ် ပုဂံ သွားတယ်။
နှစ်ရက် နေတယ်။
အရမ်း လှတယ်။ နောက်တစ်ခါ သွားချင်တယ်။

blocks.text: Notice that **not one verb above changes its form**, and only the time word in the first sentence tells us it's all in the past. This is the promise from the introduction: not a single past-tense verb table to memorize.

blocks.title: Do it today
items: Fill the five-sentence frame with a trip **you actually took** — it needn't be far; the market will do. Write it by hand, in Burmese script.
Then tell it out loud without looking at your notes. If you stumble halfway, look again, cover it, repeat. Five sentences you can say fluently are worth more than fifty you merely understand.
⚠️ When you check it over, count how many times you used ခဲ့. If it's more than once, there's probably one too many — try taking it out and read it again.
